articles.title: Elden Ring Has Quietly Become A24's Most Expensive Movie Yet
articles.summary: It's been a while since we've gotten any official updates on A24's Elden Ring movie, but a new report has revealed that the film has a massive budget. Elden Ring is certainly more expensive than any other movie the Backrooms studio has made before, so it'll be A24's first true blockbuster.
body: The Wall Street Journal published an in-depth report on A24 on Oct. 23. While it's mostly highlighting how the studio found success with Backrooms and You Can See Everything this year, it also confirms that Elden Ring has a budget close to $200 million. "A24 is currently making its most expensive movie to date—an adaptation of the video game Elden Ring scheduled for release in 2028 that costs nearly $200 million, according to people familiar with the matter," the report explains.

With that budget, Elden Ring will have far surpassed Marty Supreme to become A24's most expensive movie. A24 is reportedly worth over $3.5 billion and is looking for ways to stay independent as it grows. Putting out a blockbuster adaptation of one of the decade's most popular video games is part of that strategy.

Still, signs point to Elden Ring being more of an A24-feeling film than your typical blockbuster. It's directed by Alex Garland, who previously made movies like Ex Machina, Annihilation, and Civil War. We also know it'll star actors like Kit Connor, Cailee Spaeny, and Nick Offerman in undisclosed roles, as we're still being kept in the dark about plot details.
points: It's been a while since we've gotten any official updates on A24's Elden Ring movie, but a new report has revealed that the film has a massive budget.
Elden Ring is certainly more expensive than any other movie the Backrooms studio has made before, so it'll be A24's first true blockbuster.

articles.title: The Most Broken D&D Item Keeps Ruining Games. Here Are 3 Ways to Fix It
articles.summary: Magic items are an important component of the Dungeons & Dragons experience; collecting and using wondrous artifacts is a given in a role-playing game of heroic fantasy. This is why, in D&D, every character class has access to magic items, starting at the very first level.
body: There is a long list of legendary artifacts that could fit that description: the Staff of Power, Queen Ehlissa’s Marvelous Nightingale, and of course, the Hand and Eye of Vecna come to mind. However, none of these items of unfathomable power match the sheer annoyance caused by the humble potion of healing.

In the current version of the D&D rules, combat can be a long and grueling affair that often comes down to attrition. Even if a character is reduced to zero hit points (HP) or below, they don’t die (except in the case of Massive Damage ). Instead, they become Unconscious and start rolling death saving throws. On three failures, the character dies, while on three successes (or a natural 20 roll), they stabilize. While all this is happening, there is plenty of time for the rest of the party to administer healing, which usually comes in the form of spells or, more simply, potions. Once healed, a character can simply stand back up and join the action again.

This is why, in D&D, every character class has access to magic items, starting at the very first level.

articles.title: An officially licensed Knightmare game, based on the British TV show, is coming next year
articles.summary: A free point-and-click adventure based on Knightmare, the cult ITV children's show, is in development.
body: For the uninitiated, Knightmare aired on ITV between 1987 and 1994 and single-handedly introduced an entire generation of kids to fantasy RPGs and computer games. Sitting with Treguard, the deeply affable Dungeon Master, three kids in ironed jeans and their best button-up shirts would direct a fourth member of their team, the Dungeoneer, through a labyrinthine hand-painted dungeon, solving riddles, casting spells, and - hopefully - avoiding traps.
Interestingly, the players' life force meter - the stuff of legend of (k)nightmare fuel - has been ditched in a bid to give players the time they need to explore.

Much of its cast is returning, including Hugo Myatt as Treguard, Mark Knight as Lord Fear, Clifford Barry as Brother Strange, Edmund Dehn as Gumboil the Knight, Iona Kennedy as Greystagg, and Paul Valentine and Alec Westwood as jesters Motley and Folly, respectively.
Watson says the game's art was drawn by hand, stressing "everything you see and hear is made by real humans" (thanks, VGC ).
points: A free point-and-click adventure based on Knightmare, the cult ITV children's show, is in development.

articles.title: Steve Rogers Wields Mjolnir in the Latest Avengers: Doomsday Trailer
articles.summary: A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday dropped on Oct. 24. While it's not very long, it shows a surprising amount of new footage rather than rehashing clips we've already seen. In particular, it has some great moments featuring Captain America (all three of them).
body: Avengers: Doomsday's latest trailer starts with a pretty cool moment, as we see Steve Rogers wielding Mjölnir again. He's not doing so in battle; he simply summons it from Thor's hand, likely to prove he's the real Steve Rogers. Later on the trailer, we also see Steve Rogers holding Thor's hammer as he asks Thor if it bothers him before they travel somewhere via the Bifrost. Captain America wielding Mjölnir was one of the best parts of Avengers: Endgame, so hopefully we also see him fight with it again in Doomsday.

Between those bookending scenes with Steve Rogers and Mjolnir, we see new shots of Doctor Doom fighting, Professor X seemingly observing another world's destruction, and Invisible Woman and The Thing meeting with M'Baku and Black Panther. Then we get the trailer's funniest scene, as Ant-Man calls Steve Rogers Captain America and then stumbles through the fact that three people who have technically taken up the mantle are in the room, as Sam Wilson and John Walker are also there.

articles.title: GTA: San Andreas’ Most Frustrating MIssion Show How Far Rockstar Has Come in 22 Years
articles.summary: With the imminent release of Grand Theft Auto 6, I decided it was time to revisit what was probably the biggest game of my childhood: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. In 2005, GTA: San Andreas was one of the first four games I bought for the PlayStation 2, alongside Final Fantasy X, Kingdom Hearts…
body: Also there was no way I was playing GTA: San Andreas on a controller. Not with those controls.

But riding that bike also reminded me how roughly controlled Rockstar Games used to be. Turning the bike feels like I'm trying to drive a truck, and running around with CJ while trying to aim drove me mad more often than not as the digital avatar insisted on abruptly changing direction. Sure, playing San Andreas after witnessing how much game development and technology in general evolved over the past two decades requires some concessions, but oh my god, returning to a 22-year-old Grand Theft Auto game really puts it into perspective.

This contrast of loving the exploration and the characters while hating the controls came to a head in one mission: the “OG Loc” mission.“OG Loc” is one of the Big Smoke's missions, in which he, Sweet, and CJ go to the police station to pick up Jeffrey, an old friend of theirs. In his endless search to enter the gangster life, Jeffrey assumed a new identity, “OG Loc,” and started committing small crimes, which led him to be arrested. When in jail, Jeffrey is sexually assaulted by another inmate who, according to him, stole his rhymes.

articles.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 is more than a retread of Netflix's beloved first season - it's a story that truly understands what it means to exist in Night City
articles.summary: Last night, I sat down with a greasy pizza and a few bottles of beer and braced myself for 10 episodes of heartbreak. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' second season is out, and it follows in the footsteps of Studio Trigger's beloved, and tragic, debut. My expectations were way off.
body: Not because it wasn't good: Edgerunners Season 2 is fantastic. Packed with a wonderful cast of troubled characters, their story brought to life with gorgeous and often unorthodox animation. The soundtrack, the voice acting... Quality-wise the bar is as high as the first season. What surprised me was the decision to bring something many may find peculiar given Cyberpunk's dire setting and desperate energy. The show is hopeful. Defiant, even.

In the show's opening episode, we are introduced to characters at rock bottom. King, having suffered from cyberpsychosis, has had his augmentations stripped out of his body, and lost his home. D's in the midst of a lonely journey of revenge, while Talia is rubbing elbows with the Maelstrom gang. Roman, a 12-year-old, is broke and struggling to pursue filmmaking in a world that's left the medium behind. In the pursuit of money, he is nearly diced up.
points: Last night, I sat down with a greasy pizza and a few bottles of beer and braced myself for 10 episodes of heartbreak.
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' second season is out, and it follows in the footsteps of Studio Trigger's beloved, and tragic, debut.
Not because it wasn't good: Edgerunners Season 2 is fantastic.
Quality-wise the bar is as high as the first season.

articles.title: This third-person mod for Deus Ex turns the classic immersive sim into Max Payne, introducing dual-wielding and shoot-dodging
articles.summary: The idea of playing Deus Ex entirely in third person has always seemed like sacrilege to me. I like my immersive sims to be, well, immersive, to let me see the world through my character's eyes and interact with it up close and personal.
body: Yet having just watched several videos of Deus Ex being played in third-person, I've realised that perhaps I wouldn't be so averse to experiencing Ion Storm's cyberpunk classic from a new perspective. Especially if that new perspective involves Max Payne -style bullet dodging.

Over the last week or so, YouTuber dan2091 posted numerous videos of a WIP third-person mod for Deus Ex. Presumably, the mod is dan2091's own creation, though there's no information in the video's descriptions or the channel more generally to confirm this.

In any case, the various clips demonstrate that there's more to the mod than a simple camera shift. One video shows a system that lets JC Denton wear different clothes, making the most of the player's ability to see their own character. Another video shows bespoke ladder climbing animations, while a third showcases a new dual-wielding system. The latter functions regardless of whether the player is in first-or-third person too, which is neat.

I like my immersive sims to be, well, immersive, to let me see the world through my character's eyes and interact with it up close and personal.

articles.title: Civilization 7's game changing update was 'personally challenging' for its creative director, as being able to play as a single faction 'wasn't part of the original vision'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: The development and release of Civilization 7 has been a rollercoaster for both fans of the series and developer Firaxis. The most recent entry in the long-running 4X series shipped with an age-transition mechanic where players would switch between civilisations at multiple points during a game. It was a radical design shift that divided the community, received well by some players, but going down like a glass of cold sick with others.

Earlier this year, Firaxis introduced an update to Civilization 7 that made age transitions optional and reimplemented the traditional, single-civ mode of play. Yet according to Firaxis, this was not a decision the studio made easily, and was particularly tough for creative director Ed Beach.

"I was always frustrated by playing a Civ game and having a civilization with one period of time, where I had special abilities and special powers," Meier explains. "And for the rest of history I would just play sort of as a vanilla Civ where I didn't have anything unique about what I was doing."

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 would have let players generate alternate timelines based on their choices in previous games, according to the series' technical director
articles.summary: The more information that dribbles out from BioWare's cancelled Mass Effect game, the sadder I feel about the whole sorry situation. We've already seen an in-engine trailer that introduced a new protagonist and reintroduced Liara T'Soni, and we've heard that the game was set in a 'galactic Cold…
body: This is according to Mass Effect's Franchise Technical Director Romain Toutain, who ran a Twitch stream during which he provided commentary on the recently leaked trailer, offering some insight into the game that trailer was supposed to reveal (via Kotaku ). Although the stream was in French, a clip was posted on Bluesky by user @loustica-lucia, who added English subtitles to Toutain's commentary.

During his stream, Toutain mentions that BioWare was working on a novel way to account for the many choices players made while playing the Mass Effect trilogy, pointing out that "all of the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taking into account."

Indeed, this is partly the reason behind the cancelled successor's name as shown in the leaked internal trailer. "One of the reasons why it was called Mass Effect Universe is that you had so many choices that you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes." Toutain quickly clarifies that his explanation is "to keep it simple," adding "It's not exactly how it worked. You had different timelines, basically. You could almost generate timelines, kinda like Zero Time Dilemma."

articles.title: James Gunn Defends the DCU's Approach to Interconnected Stories, Doesn't Want Movies Like Clayface to Exist Just to 'Set Up' Crossovers
articles.summary: DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers. Clayface poured into the DCU when it brought the tragic story of Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) to theaters yesterday.
body: Despite solid scores from critics and fans (IGN gave it a 7/10 review ), there are DC watchers who have continued to complain that executives like Gunn and co-chairman Peter Safran haven't done a good job of using smaller stories to build toward bigger tie-in projects. For reference, the DCU technically started with animated series Creature Commandos before heading to theaters with Superman. Peacemaker Season 2, Supergirl, Lanterns, and Clayface then followed.

While standalone Wonder Woman and Batman movies are in the cards, projects like The People v. Gorilla Grodd seem to be further along than most, with crossover moments mostly limited so far. So, what gives? Gunn has an easy answer that might leave impatient fans wanting more, but for him, it's a solution that will keep the DCU telling quality stories for years to come.

"I couldn't agree more," he said when replying to a fan defending the cinematic universe on Threads. "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else."

articles.title: Call of Duty Movie Director Teases Story That Explores 'the Cost of War,' Praises Modern Warfare Characters
articles.summary: Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war." The filmmaker behind Skydance-Paramount's upcoming reimagining of Activision's massive first-person shooter series dived into…
body: "And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."

Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job. That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."
"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."

These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.

body: For Stop Caring, Artemis Octavio interviewed Jeremy Couillard, the multimedia artist behind such offbeat indie experiments as Soul Injector Commando: an FPS about shooting a sense of humanity into enemies based on real-life billionaires.

This past week’s discourse on gamedev team sizes, sparked by a GI.biz post about Star Wars: Galactic Racer and its "core team" of 75, was clearly an inferior rehash of the Nic-sparked Expedition 33 one last year. But it has produced this thoughtful Game Developer piece, by Bryant Francis, on whether we need a new language approach to fit recent developments in outsourcing.

When done right, the model diversifies financial risk and preserves what works about triple-A development without the need to keep everyone under one corporate entity. When done wrong, you can wind up with a game development class system, where creative direction and funding flows in limited directions, and those not lucky enough to be at the center struggle to keep doing the work they love.

articles.title: Vinland Saga’s Creator Has ‘No Good News’ On Season 3: ‘The Project Is Not Currently In Progress’
articles.summary: Is MAPPA just too busy working on Chainsaw Man and Jujutsu Kaisen, or is this a sign that a second season of Vinland Saga was a commercial flop?
body: It’s been over three years since the second season of Vinland Saga, MAPPA’s adaptation of Makoto Yukimura’s beloved historical epic manga, graced our screens, yet an animated conclusion to Thorfinn’s journey still isn’t in the cards. That’s according to Vinland Saga’s creator, who apologised to fans while confirming that a potential season 3 “is not currently in progress.”

Makoto Yukimura’s Vinland Saga is perfect. I cannot overstate this; it’s comfortably earned its spot in my top three, nestled somewhere between Mob Psycho 100 and Fullmetal Alchemist. Yukimura’s manga ended in mid-2025, after 20 years in publication, and I am so glad I got into this one late. Waiting for over a decade for Thorfinn’s story to conclude would have driven me up the wall.

Unfortunately, if you’re an anime-only watcher, I have bad news–or rather, Yukimura himself does. As spotted by OtakuKart, the author revealed in a post on X that there are currently no plans for a follow-up to MAPPA’s second season of Vinland Saga.
Sorry my friend, I have no good news about that. The project is not currently in progress.

Take up your sword, become the Hero of Time, and save the Kingdom of Hyrule in this classic tale, built from the ground up for Nintendo Switch 2.
